subject: Hosted API: data custody, retention, and deletion Q&A
messages:
From: Alice Moran <alice.moran@finosci.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: security@finosci.com
Date: 2026-09-01T15:12:00Z
Subject: Vendor questionnaire: hosted API data lifecycle

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking this. We're putting together our vendor security pack and have a short set of questions specific to data residency, retention, and deletion for Redwood's hosted API. Can you confirm the following for our record?

1) Regional residency: Can we ensure data (prompts + responses + embeddings) is stored only in a single geography (US) for our tenant? How does failover work if that region degrades?
2) Retention defaults: What is the default retention window for request logs, prompts/responses, embeddings, and backup snapshots for hosted customers? Are there per-tenant overrides?
3) Deletion mechanics: When a tenant requests an erasure, what systems are wiped (live store, cache, backups)? How do you prove deletion to us (audit logs, deletion report)?
4) Backups & replicas: Are backups or replicas ever stored outside the customer-selected region? What are the timelines for backup deletion?
5) Key management & access: Is customer data encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys? Can operations access unencrypted payloads for troubleshooting?

We're on a tight timeline; if you can share a written response and any supporting artifacts (diagram or short PDF) that'd be ideal.

Best,
Alice
Security Operations
Finosci
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Alice Moran <alice.moran@finosci.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T17:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Vendor questionnaire: hosted API data lifecycle

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Irene (security) for the technical details and Ben for commercial/contract items. High-level answers below; Irene will follow up with specifics and an attached diagram.

- Regional residency: Yes — customers can pin to a single region (e.g., us-east-1). By default we serve and store tenant data only in the selected region. In the event of region degradation we offer configurable failover policies (canary multi-region or single-region with queued requests) — failover is opt-in and requires explicit tenant consent.
- Retention defaults: Our hosted default retention for prompts+responses is 30 days; embeddings 90 days; request logs 90 days. We support per-tenant retention overrides via the Console or via your Account rep.
- Deletion mechanics: Erasure requests trigger: (1) live-tenant data purge, (2) KV/prefix caches invalidation, and (3) queued snapshot cleanup. We can produce an audit record showing timestamped deletion events.
- Backups & replicas: Backups are retained for 30 days by default and are kept only in the customer-selected region unless cross-region DR is enabled (opt-in).
- KMS & access: Data at rest is encrypted using provider-managed keys by default. Customer-managed KMS is available on Dedicated/Private; for hosted we offer Bring-Your-Own-KMS for enterprise customers (add-on). Operations-level access to plaintext payloads is tightly controlled and logged; plaintext access requires an approved runbook and is visible in audit logs.

Attachment: redwood-hosted-data-lifecycle-answer.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

Irene — can you add the details Alice requested and the architecture diagram?

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alice Moran <alice.moran@finosci.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Vendor questionnaire: hosted API data lifecycle

Hi Alice — Irene from Security here with the technical specifics. I'm including concise, auditable answers below and attaching a simple architecture diagram showing region boundaries and DR options.

1) Regional residency and failover
- Tenant data residency: When provisioning a tenant on Hosted, the tenant is assigned to a physical region (AWS region). All persistent stores (S3-equivalent object store, DB, and block volumes used by the inference runtime) are created within that region.
- Failover model:
  - Passive (single-region): No automatic cross-region replication. If the region becomes unavailable requests queue and will resume once capacity returns.
  - Active (opt-in cross-region DR): If enabled, we replicate encrypted snapshots to a secondary region in the same geopolitical boundary (e.g., us-east-1 -> us-west-2). Replication is strictly opt-in and requires explicit contractual agreement.

2) Retention windows (defaults & overrides)
- Prompts + responses (raw request/response pairs): default 30 days.
- Embeddings & derived artifacts: default 90 days.
- Request/operational logs (metadata, tracing): default 90 days.
- Snapshot/backups: rolling 30-day retention with daily snapshots; snapshot soft-delete window is 7 days (deferred deletion) after a snapshot is marked for purge.
- Per-tenant overrides: Available for hosted customers via an Account-managed configuration. Overrides are limited by operational guardrails (minimum retention floor of 7 days for some telemetry required for debugging).

3) Deletion procedure & evidencing
- Erasure workflow:
  a) Customer requests erasure via Console/API or via support case.
  b) System marks tenant data for deletion and begins staged purge: flush KV caches, delete live objects, schedule snapshot purge.
  c) Background job verifies object removal and writes a signed audit record to the tenant's audit ledger (immutable log entry including request ID, timestamp, operator id).
- Proof of deletion:
  - We provide a deletion certificate (signed audit record) showing which stores were purged and the timestamps.
  - For customers requiring enhanced evidence, we can provide time-bound S3 inventory reports and the deletion audit ledger extract.

4) Backups & cross-region replication
- By default, backups remain in-region. Cross-region replication only happens if the customer has explicitly enabled our DR replication add-on during onboarding. We will not replicate customer data across jurisdictions without written consent.

5) KMS & operational access
- Default: Provider-managed keys (AES-256) with regular rotation.
- Enterprise option: Customer-managed KMS (BYOK) for hosted (requires subscription).
- Operational access: Access to cleartext is possible only under the following conditions: documented troubleshooting runbook, explicit approval by our Security Ops, and the event is logged in the immutable audit ledger.

Attachments:
- hostedapi-architecture-diagram.png (PNG, 120KB)

If you have specific evidence format requirements (CSV, signed PDF, SIEM ingest), tell us and we will package the audit extracts accordingly.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Head of Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Alice Moran <alice.moran@finosci.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T14:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Vendor questionnaire: hosted API data lifecycle

Thanks Irene — that clarifies a lot. Two follow-ups:

1) Deletion proof: Can you confirm the deletion certificate includes the immutable audit ledger entry ID and the list of object keys deleted? We need to show a chain of custody to our privacy office.
2) Cross-region opt-in: For our use case we will not enable cross-region DR. Please confirm that enabling analytics features will not implicitly replicate embeddings to other services hosted in different regions.

If it's easier, we can take a 30-minute call — otherwise a short confirmation here is fine.

Thanks,
Alice
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Alice Moran <alice.moran@finosci.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Vendor questionnaire: hosted API data lifecycle

Hi Alice — quick confirmations below and next steps: 

- Deletion certificate contents: Yes — the certificate includes the immutable audit ledger entry ID, request ID, and an object key manifest (list of keys/prefixes purged). For high-assurance customers we can sign the manifest and provide a time-stamped PDF.
- Analytics & replication: Analytics jobs run within the tenant's selected region for hosted customers by default. We do not implicitly replicate embeddings or request payloads to analytics pipelines in other regions. Any cross-region pipeline requires explicit opt-in and is surfaced in the Console.

Related links: https://redwood.com/docs/hosted-data-lifecycle (detailed docs)
DocuSign: docusign://DPA-98765 (if you need an updated DPA for BYOK/DR options)

If helpful, Ben can schedule a 30-minute run-through and we can include a short demo of the Console retention controls.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
